summary: First-iteration testing of Voltpay payment platform. Built /app/backend/tests/test_voltpay_backend.py with 30 pytest cases covering auth, api-keys, public /api/v1/payment_intents (create/confirm with 4242 + 4000 0002), idempotency, refunds (full/partial), customers, webhooks, checkout sessions, balance/ledger/stats. 29/30 backend tests PASS. One backend bug found: brute-force lockout never returns 429 (HTTPException is swallowed by a bare `except Exception: pass`). Frontend E2E: landing renders, /register creates account & redirects to /dashboard, sidebar nav works, API keys page shows masked secret + reveal/copy/rotate UI, Payments page loads, hosted checkout at /checkout/{token} successfully processed 4242 and reached 'Payment received' screen.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout never triggers. In routes_auth.py line 73-83, the `if (now - last_dt).total_seconds() < 900: raise HTTPException(429)` is wrapped in `try/except Exception: pass`, which catches the very HTTPException that should propagate. After 5+ failed logins, the response stays 401 instead of 429. Confirmed with 6 sequential bad logins → all 401. Fix: change to `except (ValueError, TypeError):` or move the HTTPException raise OUT of the try block.

issues: Recharts emits warnings 'width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' on first paint — ResponsiveContainer parent collapses to 0 briefly. Chart still renders. Add minHeight or fixed height to the chart container to silence warning and avoid layout shift.
Two 401 console errors from /api/auth/me on initial load (AuthContext probes session). Cosmetic — consider suppressing 401 logs for the auth probe or checking cookie first.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout in /app/backend/routes_auth.py: remove the bare `except Exception: pass` around the HTTPException(429) raise, or re-raise HTTPException explicitly. Current code lets attackers try unlimited passwords.
Optional: add minHeight to dashboard revenue chart ResponsiveContainer to silence recharts width/height warnings.

rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force lockout RCA: In /app/backend/routes_auth.py login handler, lines ~73-83: code reads last_attempt timestamp and raises HTTPException(429) inside a try block whose except catches `Exception`. Because Starlette's HTTPException inherits from Exception, the 429 is silently swallowed and execution continues to the normal password-check path, which raises 401. Reproduction: register fresh user, POST /api/auth/login 6+ times with wrong password → all return 401. Mitigation: replace `except Exception:` with a narrow `except (ValueError, TypeError):` so only datetime parsing errors are ignored, OR move the `raise HTTPException` AFTER/outside the try.
